script: Did you know true stories activate parts of your brain no other narrative can? When you hear a true story, your brain lights up differently. Neuroscientists found that factual narratives trigger increased oxytocin release – the "trust" hormone. This isn't just about entertainment; it's about survival. Our brains evolved to learn from real-life experiences, fostering empathy and social bonding. Fiction is fun, but true accounts tap into a deeper, more primal part of our psyche. They make us more connected, more likely to remember details, and even more persuaded by the message. This incredible neurological response is precisely why true stories activate parts of your brain no other narrative can.
